title: Sell Mineral Rights in Campbell County, WY
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Campbell County, WY
metaDescription: Own mineral rights in Campbell County, WY? Gillette-area CBM boom-and-bust, coal split estate, and horizontal Niobrara/Turner activity, get a real read here.
heroLead: Campbell County has three distinct mineral stories layered on top of each other around Gillette, coal, coalbed methane, and now horizontal oil, and knowing which one your interest belongs to changes everything about how I'd price it.
intro: This is the country's largest coal-producing county, home to massive surface mines like Black Thunder and North Antelope Rochelle that supply a meaningful share of the nation's thermal coal. But Campbell County's oil and gas history runs just as deep: it was ground zero for the Powder River Basin's coalbed methane boom in the late 1990s and 2000s, when thousands of shallow wells were drilled to produce methane trapped in the basin's coal seams, before low gas prices collapsed that economics and left a lot of it plugged or idle.

More recently, operators including EOG Resources and others have targeted deeper, stacked conventional and unconventional zones, the Niobrara, Turner, Sussex, Parkman, and Frontier formations, with horizontal wells and dense multi-well pad development around Gillette and Wright. If you're holding a Campbell County mineral interest, I need to know which of these three stories, coal, CBM, or the newer stacked-lateral oil plays, actually applies to your specific tract before I can give you an honest number.

sections.heading: Coal and split estate
paragraphs: Campbell County's surface coal mines operate under a split-estate arrangement that's different from oil and gas leasing: much of the coal itself is federally owned and leased through the Bureau of Land Management, while private surface owners negotiate separate surface-use agreements with the mining companies. If your family's mineral interest includes coal rights specifically, that's typically a separate legal question from oil and gas rights on the same or adjacent land, and I'll help you understand which you actually hold.
Most of what I buy and sell day to day is oil and gas mineral interest, not coal, but I always check what's actually described in your deed before assuming.

sections.heading: The coalbed methane boom and bust
paragraphs: CBM wells here produced water first, then ramping gas, from thousands of shallow completions across the basin through the 2000s. When gas prices fell, a large share of those wells stopped being economic, and many were plugged well before their coal seam reserves were exhausted. If your royalty checks from a CBM well slowed to nothing years ago, that's an extremely common story in this county, not a sign your interest lacks value entirely.
I check the specific well's plugged or idle status through state records before pricing a dormant CBM interest, since a plugged well and a temporarily idle one are priced very differently.

sections.heading: Stacked-lateral horizontal development
paragraphs: Beneath the CBM-era wellbores, operators have spent the last decade-plus drilling horizontal laterals through multiple stacked formations, the Niobrara, Turner, Sussex, Parkman, and Frontier, sometimes from the same well pad targeting different zones. This is genuinely active, ongoing development in parts of the county, particularly around Gillette and south toward Wright, and interests inside these units can carry real current royalty income.
Spacing and unitization on these stacked plays tend to be denser than older conventional development, which affects how your net mineral acreage translates into your actual royalty share.

sections.heading: Confirming which story is yours
paragraphs: I pull the Campbell County recorder's lease and deed history for your specific section, cross-reference well status through the Wyoming Oil and Gas Conservation Commission, and identify whether your interest sits in a coal-only area, a dormant CBM unit, an active stacked-lateral development, or genuinely undeveloped acreage. Only then do I quote a number, and I'll explain exactly which category yours falls into and why.

sections.heading: Why Gillette records take longer to sort out
paragraphs: Because this county has seen three distinct waves of mineral development layered on top of each other, coal leasing in the mid-twentieth century, CBM in the 2000s, and stacked-lateral horizontal drilling more recently, the paper trail on a given tract can run long. I've traced Campbell County interests through lease assignments that changed hands four or five times as operators consolidated, sold off, or exited the basin entirely during the CBM downturn.

That complexity is exactly why I don't quote a Campbell County interest sight unseen. Every layer of history matters to getting the number right, and skipping the research just shifts the risk onto you.

faqs.question: My CBM royalty checks stopped years ago. Is that interest worth anything now?
faqs.answer: Yes, though it's priced differently than active production. I'll check the well's plugged status and any redevelopment potential before quoting.

faqs.question: Do I own coal rights or oil and gas rights, or both?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on your deed language. I'll review what you have and tell you clearly which mineral rights you actually hold.

faqs.question: Is there active drilling in Campbell County right now?
faqs.answer: Yes, horizontal development in the Niobrara, Turner, and other stacked zones continues in parts of the county, particularly toward Wright. I'll check your specific section.

faqs.question: How do surface coal mines affect my mineral interest?
faqs.answer: Only if your interest overlaps an active or permitted coal mine boundary, and even then the effect depends on your specific deed and surface-use agreements. I'll clarify your situation.

faqs.question: What's the difference in how you'd price a coal interest versus an oil and gas interest?
faqs.answer: Coal is typically leased through federal or long-term royalty structures tied to production volume, while oil and gas prices against decline curves and current commodity markets. I only buy oil and gas minerals, and I'll tell you plainly if your interest is coal instead.
